newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shuttle crew chats with space station Mir.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shuttle crew chats with space station Mir.

text.p: The crew of the U.S. space shuttle Columbia got an invitation to tea on Tuesday from British-born astronaut Michael Foale aboard the troubled Russian Mir space station.
The two spaceships were linked by radio for about 10 minutes as they orbited high above North and Central America.

"We'd like to invite you to space station Mir," a cheerful Foale told the shuttle crew. "We have tea, we have coffee, we have chocolates, candy, in fact we have everything here on space station Mir that you would want."
Foale said it felt like Christmas aboard Mir as the station's crew unpacked supplies from the Progress cargo craft that docked with the orbiting outpost on Monday.

The unmanned ship brought replacements for some of Foale's personal belongings lost when an errant cargo craft slammed into the station last month. It also carried gifts from his family and a special English treat.
"I'm enjoying the first cup of tea I've had in about two months," said the 40-year-old astronaut, who grew up in Cambridge, England.
The crew of Columbia were a week into a 16-day science mission to study the behaviour of fire in space and develop new alloys. Foale is not due back on Earth until September.
